source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Use the Sun's highest position or the shortest shadow on successive days to measure a day of nearly 24 hours.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Sun is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A vertical stick's shortest shadow is used to locate the Sun's highest position during the day.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: shortest shadow marks the Sun's highest position -> successive highest positions happens first, and that produces Sun's apparent daily motion repeats.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when A vertical stick's shortest shadow is used to locate the Sun's highest position during the day is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: The mean solar day is the average time from the Sun's highest position on one day to its highest position on the next day, and it is 24 hours. Sun's apparent daily motion repeats -> shortest shadow marks the Sun's highest position -> successive highest positions give the duration of a day. The learner correctly applies this rule: The mean solar day is the average time from the Sun's highest position on one day to its highest position on the next day, and it is 24 hours. A day is just the clock label around noon, so the shadow activity does not need a shortest-shadow comparison.
